Hi Eleanor / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — appreciate the clarity on the product goals and where inference is currently a blocker. Quick recap from our side so we have a clear set of technical questions and proposed next steps. I tried to separate customer-facing requirements from what we'd need to validate in a tech deep-dive.

Key pain points you described
- User-facing chat latency above target when load spikes (~P95 observed ~350ms currently)
- Cost for inference at scale is growing faster than traffic growth (no steady cost control knobs)
- Multi-variant model testing is hard in prod (no easy routing/fallbacks)

Goals you called out
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for standard chat flows (512 token windows)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 qps (messages/s) in normal hours, burst to 500 qps during peak marketing campaigns
- Keep per-1000-token cost below current baseline (TBD) while maintaining model quality

Open technical questions we need to confirm on the deep-dive
1) Model family for production: you mentioned fine-tuning a LLaMA-derived 70B; is that the canonical model or will you evaluate 2 smaller quantized variants in parallel?
2) Typical prompt+response token lengths (avg / p95) — helps sizing KV cache and batch windows.
3) Are sessions sticky to user IDs (i.e., can we cache per-session KV cache) or do you require full cold-starts for each request?
4) Networking: Do you prefer deployment in your VPC (Private) or Redwood Dedicated in us-west for a POC?

Proposed initial topology (we'll iterate with your infra team)
- Dedicated GPU pool (us-west) for the POC with autoscaling and a smaller private variant for compliance-critical flows.
- Enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts and session KV caching for active conversations.
- Two model variants behind a routing policy: 70B q4o (high quality) and 7B fp16 (fallback during large bursts) with automated fallback thresholds.

Next steps (can action these in the next 72 hours)
- You: share the production profile CSV + a representative prompt set (redacted) — I attached a sample template.
- Us (Redwood): put together a POC scope, estimate for capacity/cost, and a deployment sketch for your review.
- Schedule: propose a technical deep-dive with your infra/CloudOps next week (30–60m) to lock down topology and access requirements.

Attachments: arboretum-production-profile.csv (template)

I'll loop in Monica and Karthik for sizing and a rough cost sketch after you share the profile.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

1) Model family: we are testing a fine-tuned LLaMA-70B variant for highest fidelity, but we'd like to run a smaller quantized 13B/Q4 variant in parallel for conversational fallbacks. The 70B is the canonical "primary" model for now.
2) Token lengths: avg request (prompt+response) ~ 320 tokens; p95 ~ 820 tokens during longer diagnostic sessions.
3) Sessions: yes, sessions are sticky to user IDs for signed-in customers — we expect KV cache per session to be beneficial.
4) Networking: for the POC we prefer Redwood Dedicated in us-west; long-term we may evaluate a Private (VPC) setup. For now, Dedicated is fine.

Additional constraints
- GDPR-sensitive pseudonymized data on some records — we won't share full raw PII in the POC.
- Burst patterns: marketing campaigns create short 10–20 minute bursts ~400–600 qps with ~10% sustained for up to 45 minutes.

I've attached the production profile CSV (redacted) and a short notes doc. Happy to schedule the deep-dive — our infra lead (Tom) is available Thu 3/21 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 3/22 13:00–14:00 PT.

Quick technical sketch from my side — high-level numbers and recommendations so we can put something in the POC doc:

Assumptions based on their profile + our runtime measurements with similar models:
- Primary: LLaMA-70B q4o-ish quantized (KV cache enabled)
- Fallback: 13B q4 (quantized) or 7B fp16 for the cheapest low-latency fallback
- Avg token payload: 320 tokens; p95 tokens ~820

Estimated throughput / GPU (rough):
- 70B q4o on A100-80GB (or equivalent): ~18–22 tokens/ms => ~18k–22k tokens/s -> with avg 320 tokens/request => ~56–68 reqs/s per GPU in steady-state. With batching and kernel tuning could be 10–20% better.
- 13B q4 on 80GB: ~60–80 reqs/s (avg 320 tokens)

Sizing for their targets (200 qps sustained, 600 qps burst):
- Primary pool (70B): to handle 200 qps steady with headroom, 4 GPUs (gives ~224–272 reqs/s). For bursts, rely on routing to fallback + autoscale to add 2–3 GPUs (lead time ~45–90s) and pre-warm policy tied to campaign windows.
- Fallback pool (13B): 3 GPUs should absorb most burst overflow (adds ~180–240 reqs/s). Combined routing should keep P95 <120ms if KV cache hit rates are high (~>35%) and batching windows are tuned to 20–30ms.

Performance levers and immediate actions:
1) KV cache: enable per-session KV with eviction after 30m idle — should reduce tokens generated and improve latency for repeat interactions.
2) Batching: use adaptive batching with 20–30ms max latency window for foreground chat; offline/batch jobs can use bigger windows.
3) Route policy: primary first, if queueing latency > 80ms then shift new requests to 13B fallback for that session.
4) Quantization: recommend q4o for 70B for POC; evaluate model quality diff vs fp16.

POC plan items I can deliver in 3 business days:
- Concrete GPU counts and memory maps for Dedicated us-west.
- Initial config for adaptive batching + autoscale thresholds.
- A short runbook describing warm-up and fallback behavior.

I'll prepare the numbers and a cost overlay for Monica to merge into the proposal.

-Karthik
